overall: The AG found the Nantucket Offshore Wind Work Group was not a public body under the Open Meeting Law because it was not empowered to act collectively, so no violation was found and the notice and timeliness issues were not reached.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the offshore wind work group was a public body that violated the Open Meeting Law, including by failing to post meeting notices.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we find that the Group was not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The group failed the second public-body factor because it was not empowered to act collectively, so it had no set membership, no votes, and no quorum.
allegations.key_passage: Applying the second of these three factors, we find that the Group was not a public body because it was not empowered to act collectively.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the group failed to post notices of its meetings as the Open Meeting Law requires.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we need not address the first and third factors, and we conclude that the Group was not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Town argued the complaint was untimely as to all meetings except May 1; the AG did not reach this argument.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find that the Group was not a public body, we do not address the Town’s argument that the complaint is untimely as to all meetings except that of May 1.
